edges.description: Loss of ALG12 alpha1,6-mannosyltransferase activity blocks addition of the eighth mannose to the dolichol-linked GlcNAc2Man7 intermediate, impairing completion of the N-glycan precursor used for transfer to proteins.

The precursor-assembly defect alters N-glycosylation-site occupancy and downstream glycan processing, producing abnormal total-serum and IgG N-glycan profiles; the intervening transfer and processing steps make this an indirect biochemical link.
intermediate_mechanisms: Transfer of incomplete lipid-linked oligosaccharides, reduced protein N-glycosylation-site occupancy, and downstream glycan processing.

edges.description: Reduced N-glycosylation-site occupancy and abnormal glycan processing disrupt the folding, trafficking, and function of many glycoproteins, producing systemic dysfunction through incompletely resolved protein- and tissue-specific intermediates.
Multisystem glycoprotein dysfunction is associated with neurologic and brain manifestations, but the affected glycoproteins and intervening developmental pathways are unresolved.
Multisystem ALG12-CDG is associated with impaired growth and feeding; the glycoprotein and tissue-specific intermediates are unresolved.
Multisystem ALG12-CDG is associated with craniofacial dysmorphism and male genital hypoplasia through unresolved developmental intermediates.
Rare severe prenatal or neonatal reports associate ALG12-CDG with renal and skeletal developmental abnormalities through unknown intermediates.
Ventricular septal defect and severe scoliosis co-occurred in one exceptional adult, but their relationship to ALG12 dysfunction is unknown and confounded by coexisting variants.
Abnormal IgG N-glycosylation and low serum immunoglobulins co-occur in ALG12-CDG, but the evidence does not establish that the glycan-profile abnormality directly causes the decreased concentration.

Recurrent infections co-occur with low immunoglobulins and abnormal IgG glycosylation, but the evidence does not establish a causal path from the measured glycan abnormality to infection susceptibility.
Hypoglycosylation and deficiency of factor XI provide a known protein-level intermediate linking systemic glycosylation abnormalities to an abnormal coagulation phenotype.
intermediate_mechanisms: Hypoglycosylation and deficiency of coagulation factor XI.

edges.description: Developmental delay is part of the reported ALG12-CDG neurologic spectrum.
Intellectual disability is part of the reported ALG12-CDG neurologic spectrum.
Hypotonia is part of the reported ALG12-CDG neurologic spectrum.
Failure to thrive is a reported growth manifestation of ALG12-CDG.
Short stature is a reported growth manifestation of ALG12-CDG.
Dysmorphic features include craniofacial involvement.
Male genital hypoplasia is a genitourinary developmental manifestation.
Skeletal dysplasia-like abnormalities are part of the severe neonatal branch.
Multicystic kidneys expand the renal phenotype of severe ALG12-CDG.
Ventricular septal defect was reported in one exceptional adult, but attribution to ALG12 deficiency is unknown and confounded by coexisting ALG6 and KMT2D variants.
Severe scoliosis was reported in one exceptional adult, but attribution to ALG12 deficiency is unknown and confounded by coexisting ALG6 and KMT2D variants.
A type I transferrin hypoglycosylation pattern reports impaired N-glycosylation-site occupancy downstream of the ALG12 precursor defect.
Accumulation of GlcNAc2Man5-7 with reduced GlcNAc2Man8-9 reports impaired ALG12 enzymatic activity.
Hypoglycosylated coagulation proteins report systemic plasma-protein hypoglycosylation caused by the ALG12-CDG glycosylation defect.
